title: tests.py's conftest docstring and code.md's Git in tests say --dist load hands tests in small consecutive chunks, not one at a time
goal: _tools/conftest.py's SLOW_FIRST docstring and kb/_self/code.md's Git in tests section describe --dist load as the pinned pytest-xdist 3.8.0 load.py does (consecutive chunks, a first chunk of at least two, no file or class kept on one worker), not as one test at a time, so the docs no longer contradict kb/public/python/pytest-xdist.md

run: import subprocess,sys;p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'_tools/selfdoc.py','section','code','Git in tests'],capture_output=True,text=True);t=p.stdout+open('_tools/conftest.py').read();sys.exit(1 if p.returncode or 'Git in tests' not in p.stdout or 'one at a time' in t else 0)

notes: Found by the SP-ofvvong6 review (fresh-context reviewer, 2026-10-14): research ST-sxf575kx showed --dist load sends consecutive chunks (first chunk max(min(len//workers//4, maxschedchunk), 2) = 2 at 112 tests on 12 workers); even --maxschedchunk 1 keeps a first chunk of 2, so rewording is the fix, not a new flag. _tools/conftest.py:55-57 and kb/_self/code.md:26 still say one at a time.
